::: {#def-let}
#### `let`

The Racket expression

```racket
(let ([name1 e1]
      ...
      [namen en])
  body)
```

evaluates `e1`, ..., `en`,
gives each value its name,
and returns the value of `body`, which can use those names.
The names last only inside `body`.

A `let` expression is shorthand for applying a `lambda` expression (@def-lambda):
it has the same value as `((lambda (name1 ... namen) body) e1 ... en)`.
So `(let ([s (+ 1 2)]) (* s s))` and `((lambda (s) (* s s)) (+ 1 2))` both return 9.

:::

*Video:* Cain uses `let` to save a result that would otherwise be computed twice, and shows how `let` becomes a `lambda`, in [CS 107 Lecture 22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3LeCydausnk) [@cain2008cs107videos].
